title: Who Picks the Direction
endLine: Speed one enzyme, slow its opposite, and one direction wins.

scenes.tts: The first film ended on a problem. Both pathways run downhill, so one liver cell could run them both at once. Now meet two near-twin molecules. Fructose one, six bisphosphate is a step on the road to glucose. Fructose two, six bisphosphate is on neither road. So why does the liver make it?
scenes.narration: The first film ended on a problem. Both pathways run downhill, so one liver cell could run them both at once. Now meet two near-twin molecules. Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is a step on the road to glucose. Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate is on neither road. So why does the liver make it?
scenes.caption: The first film ended on a problem. Both pathways run downhill, so one liver cell could run them both at once. Now meet two near-twin molecules. Fructose-1,6-bisphosphate is a step on the road to glucose. Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate is on neither road. So why does the liver make it?
scenes.visual: Continue the first film's 16:9 world and COLOUR MAP without a reset: BLUE = glycolysis and its enzymes; ORANGE = gluconeogenesis and its bypass enzymes; YELLOW = glucose and the carbon intermediates (the cargo that moves); GREEN = ATP / GTP high-energy phosphates; RED = one-way wall / wasted heat; GREY = structure; TEXT = neutral labels. NEW in this film, carried to the end: MAGENTA = fructose-2,6-bisphosphate, the regulator; a small WHITE 'P' tag = a phosphate added to a protein. THE WORLD, kept all film: a GREY liver-cell outline fills about 80% of the frame height. Inside it, the first film's two-lane road runs vertically between a YELLOW 'glucose' chip at the top and a YELLOW '2 pyruvate' chip at the bottom: the LEFT lane is BLUE with downward arrows ('glycolysis'), the RIGHT lane is ORANGE with upward arrows ('gluconeogenesis'). Three 'stations' cross the road at the first film's three cliffs (top, middle, bottom); at each a BLUE gate sits on the left lane and an ORANGE gate on the right. A small 'schematic' tag sits bottom right all film. During the first two sentences, YELLOW dots run down the BLUE lane and up the ORANGE lane at the same time and circle round and round the road; a small GOLD tag 'both downhill' (the first film's closing words) glows at the top. On 'two near-twin molecules', the camera slides to the MIDDLE station and two large chips appear side by side: a YELLOW chip 'fructose-1,6-bisphosphate' sitting ON the road, and a MAGENTA chip 'fructose-2,6-bisphosphate' hovering just beside it. On 'step on the road', YELLOW dots pass through the yellow chip. On 'on neither road', the MAGENTA chip bobs between the two lanes, touching neither. On the question, large white text across the top: 'Why make it at all?'

Title 'Who Picks the Direction' fades in above the road for 2 s while the question text fades out. The MAGENTA chip shrinks to a small token parked at the right edge of the cell (it returns in s06). YELLOW dots keep circling both lanes.

scenes.tts: First, the stakes. At each one-way step, the two pathways use opposing enzymes, a pair. Run both at full speed, and glucose is broken down and rebuilt for nothing. How many high-energy phosphates does one turn waste?
scenes.narration: First, the stakes. At each one-way step, the two pathways use opposing enzymes, a pair. Run both at full speed, and glucose is broken down and rebuilt for nothing. How many high-energy phosphates does one turn waste?
scenes.caption: First, the stakes. At each one-way step, the two pathways use opposing enzymes, a pair. Run both at full speed, and glucose is broken down and rebuilt for nothing. How many high-energy phosphates does one turn waste?
scenes.visual: Pull back so the whole road and all three stations fill the cell. On 'opposing enzymes, a pair', each station pulses in turn, top to bottom, with its BLUE and ORANGE gates lighting together, and a label appears beside each: 'glucose pair', 'middle pair', 'pyruvate pair'. On 'full speed', YELLOW dots race down the BLUE lane and straight back up the ORANGE lane in a fast loop; a counter at the right reads 'glucose made: 0'. On the question, the counter is replaced by a RED box 'wasted per turn: ?' and white question text across the top: 'Phosphates wasted per turn?'
Deliberate thinking pause. Hold the question text and the RED 'wasted per turn: ?' box. YELLOW dots keep looping slowly round the road; the '?' flickers gently. No other change.

scenes.tts: Four. Rebuilding spends six, and breaking down returns only two. One is lost at the glucose pair, one at the middle pair, and two at the pyruvate pair. All of it ends as heat.
scenes.narration: Four. Rebuilding spends six, and breaking down returns only two. One is lost at the glucose pair, one at the middle pair, and two at the pyruvate pair. All of it ends as heat.
scenes.caption: Four. Rebuilding spends six, and breaking down returns only two. One is lost at the glucose pair, one at the middle pair, and two at the pyruvate pair. All of it ends as heat.
scenes.visual: Question text dissolves; the box now reads 'wasted per turn: 4'. Counts computed from the lesson (6 spent, 2 returned, 6 - 2 = 4). On 'rebuilding spends six', six GREEN chips (no text inside, or 'ATP'/'GTP' at size 24) stack beside the ORANGE lane. On 'returns only two', two GREEN chips appear beside the BLUE lane, slide across and cancel two of the six; four GREEN chips remain. On 'one at the glucose pair', one GREEN chip flies to the top station; on 'one at the middle pair', one to the middle station; on 'two at the pyruvate pair', two to the bottom station. On 'heat', each of the four turns into RED wavy heat lines rising out of the cell. The YELLOW loop keeps running.

scenes.tts: Now zoom in on the middle pair. P F K one puts a phosphate on, making fructose one, six bisphosphate. F B P ase one cuts that phosphate back off. Both enzymes work in the same liver cell.
scenes.narration: Now zoom in on the middle pair. PFK-1 puts a phosphate on, making fructose-1,6-bisphosphate. FBPase-1 cuts that phosphate back off. Both enzymes work in the same liver cell.
scenes.caption: Now zoom in on the middle pair. PFK-1 puts a phosphate on, making fructose-1,6-bisphosphate. FBPase-1 cuts that phosphate back off. Both enzymes work in the same liver cell.
scenes.visual: The heat lines fade. The camera zooms into the MIDDLE station until it fills about 65% of the frame height. Upper YELLOW chip 'fructose-6-phosphate', lower YELLOW chip 'fructose-1,6-bisphosphate' (glucose is up, pyruvate is down, as in the first film). BLUE gate on the left lane labelled 'PFK-1'; ORANGE gate on the right lane labelled 'FBPase-1'. On 'puts a phosphate on', a YELLOW dot passes down through the BLUE gate, the upper chip briefly copies itself into the lower chip. On 'cuts that phosphate back off', a YELLOW dot passes up through the ORANGE gate from the lower chip to the upper. On 'same liver cell', the GREY cell edge visible behind both gates pulses once; both gates glow equally and dots keep passing both ways at equal rates.

scenes.tts: This is where the twin comes in. Fructose two, six bisphosphate speeds up P F K one and slows F B P ase one. One molecule, opposite effects. One, six is the pathway. Two, six is the regulator.
scenes.narration: This is where the twin comes in. Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate speeds up PFK-1 and slows FBPase-1. One molecule, opposite effects. One, six is the pathway. Two, six is the regulator.
scenes.caption: This is where the twin comes in. Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate speeds up PFK-1 and slows FBPase-1. One molecule, opposite effects. One, six is the pathway. Two, six is the regulator.
scenes.visual: The MAGENTA token parked since s01 grows back into the MAGENTA chip 'fructose-2,6-bisphosphate' and drifts in between the lanes. On 'speeds up PFK-1', small MAGENTA tokens dock on the BLUE gate; it widens and YELLOW dots stream down through it faster; a '+' appears beside it. On 'slows FBPase-1', MAGENTA tokens dock on the ORANGE gate; it narrows and its upward stream thins to a trickle; a '-' appears beside it. On 'One, six is the pathway', a label '1,6 = pathway' appears under the YELLOW 'fructose-1,6-bisphosphate' chip; on 'Two, six is the regulator', a label '2,6 = regulator' appears under the MAGENTA chip. Direction only: no rates or numbers.

scenes.tts: So here is the one idea. Both pathways run downhill, so energy cannot choose the direction. The cell chooses by regulation. It turns one enzyme of a pair up and its opposite down.
scenes.narration: So here is the one idea. Both pathways run downhill, so energy cannot choose the direction. The cell chooses by regulation. It turns one enzyme of a pair up and its opposite down.
scenes.caption: So here is the one idea. Both pathways run downhill, so energy cannot choose the direction. The cell chooses by regulation. It turns one enzyme of a pair up and its opposite down.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full road with all three stations; the middle station keeps its MAGENTA tokens. Large text across the top: 'Downhill both ways: the cell chooses'. On 'energy cannot choose', the GOLD 'both downhill' tag from s00 pulses and both lanes glow equally. On 'turns one enzyme of a pair up and its opposite down', at each station in turn one gate brightens and widens while its partner dims and narrows (schematic; no mechanism shown at the top and bottom stations). The YELLOW loop slows as one lane at each station gives way.

scenes.tts: Who sets the level of that regulator? A single protein with two halves. Its kinase half makes fructose two, six bisphosphate. Its phosphatase half destroys it. Whichever half wins sets the level.
scenes.narration: Who sets the level of that regulator? A single protein with two halves. Its kinase half makes fructose-2,6-bisphosphate. Its phosphatase half destroys it. Whichever half wins sets the level.
scenes.caption: Who sets the level of that regulator? A single protein with two halves. Its kinase half makes fructose-2,6-bisphosphate. Its phosphatase half destroys it. Whichever half wins sets the level.
scenes.visual: Zoom back to the middle station, which shifts left to the left 55% of the frame. At right, a large two-lobed TEXT-outlined shape appears, one protein, labelled 'one protein' (a cartoon, not a structure). Its left lobe is labelled 'kinase half', its right lobe 'phosphatase half'. On 'makes', the kinase lobe glows and puffs out MAGENTA tokens that drift toward the middle station. On 'destroys it', the phosphatase lobe glows and swallows nearby MAGENTA tokens, which pop and vanish. A vertical MAGENTA gauge between protein and station, labelled '2,6 level', rises when the kinase lobe glows and falls when the phosphatase lobe glows. Gauge has no numbers (schematic).

scenes.tts: After a meal, insulin keeps this protein free of an added phosphate. The kinase half wins, and fructose two, six bisphosphate rises. P F K one speeds up, F B P ase one slows, and glycolysis runs.
scenes.narration: After a meal, insulin keeps this protein free of an added phosphate. The kinase half wins, and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate rises. PFK-1 speeds up, FBPase-1 slows, and glycolysis runs.
scenes.caption: After a meal, insulin keeps this protein free of an added phosphate. The kinase half wins, and fructose-2,6-bisphosphate rises. PFK-1 speeds up, FBPase-1 slows, and glycolysis runs.
scenes.visual: A tag at top left: 'after a meal'. A TEXT chip 'insulin' appears at the frame edge, outside the cell, and sends a signal arrow toward the protein (insulin never touches it); the protein carries NO white 'P' tag. On 'kinase half wins', the kinase lobe glows steadily and the phosphatase lobe dims. On 'rises', the MAGENTA gauge climbs high and MAGENTA tokens dock on both gates of the middle station. On 'PFK-1 speeds up', the BLUE gate widens and YELLOW dots stream down it; on 'FBPase-1 slows', the ORANGE gate narrows to a trickle. On 'glycolysis runs', the whole BLUE lane brightens.

scenes.tts: In a fast, glucagon takes over. Working through P K A, it adds a phosphate to the same protein. Now the phosphatase half wins. Fructose two, six bisphosphate is destroyed, and F B P ase one runs.
scenes.narration: In a fast, glucagon takes over. Working through PKA, it adds a phosphate to the same protein. Now the phosphatase half wins. Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate is destroyed, and FBPase-1 runs.
scenes.caption: In a fast, glucagon takes over. Working through PKA, it adds a phosphate to the same protein. Now the phosphatase half wins. Fructose-2,6-bisphosphate is destroyed, and FBPase-1 runs.
scenes.visual: The tag morphs to 'in a fast'. At the frame edge, outside the cell, the 'insulin' chip slides away and a TEXT chip 'glucagon' takes its place. On 'Working through PKA', a signal arrow from glucagon lights a small TEXT chip 'PKA' inside the cell, which moves to the protein and, on 'adds a phosphate', stamps a WHITE 'P' tag onto the protein, where it stays. On 'phosphatase half wins', the phosphatase lobe glows and the kinase lobe dims. On 'destroyed', MAGENTA tokens leave both gates, are swallowed and pop; the MAGENTA gauge falls to the bottom. On 'FBPase-1 runs', the ORANGE gate widens and YELLOW dots stream up it, while the BLUE gate narrows. Same protein, same gates as s09: only the switch has changed.

scenes.tts: The pyruvate pair and the glucose pair have controls of their own. Together, in a healthy liver cell, one direction dominates, and the waste stays small.
scenes.narration: The pyruvate pair and the glucose pair have controls of their own. Together, in a healthy liver cell, one direction dominates, and the waste stays small.
scenes.caption: The pyruvate pair and the glucose pair have controls of their own. Together, in a healthy liver cell, one direction dominates, and the waste stays small.
scenes.visual: Pull back to the full road. The protein shrinks to a small icon with its WHITE 'P' tag beside the middle station, which stays set toward ORANGE. On 'controls of their own', a small tag 'own controls' appears beside the top and bottom stations (no mechanism shown). On 'one direction dominates', YELLOW traffic flows mostly up the ORANGE lane, with only a thin trickle down the BLUE lane. On 'waste stays small', a single faint RED heat wisp rises and fades (compare the four in s04); label 'waste stays small'.

scenes.tts: So direction is not set by which enzymes are present. Both sides of the pair are there. Downhill made both roads possible. Regulation decides which one carries the traffic.
scenes.narration: So direction is not set by which enzymes are present. Both sides of the pair are there. Downhill made both roads possible. Regulation decides which one carries the traffic.
scenes.caption: So direction is not set by which enzymes are present. Both sides of the pair are there. Downhill made both roads possible. Regulation decides which one carries the traffic.
scenes.visual: On 'not set by which enzymes are present', all six gates (three BLUE, three ORANGE) pulse together; none disappears. On 'Downhill made both roads possible', both lanes glow equally with the GOLD 'both downhill' tag. On 'Regulation decides', the middle-station gauge swings up (MAGENTA high) and the traffic flips to the BLUE lane, then swings down and the traffic flips back to the ORANGE lane: the same gates, run either way by the switch.

End card over the dimmed but still moving road: YELLOW dots flow up the ORANGE lane, the MAGENTA gauge hovers low, the protein icon wears its WHITE 'P' tag. Large white text, centred: 'Speed one enzyme, slow its opposite, and one direction wins.'
